# Conditional Process Plan

Shared planning logic that extends Connection Planning Functions with a conditional payment-process gate. It produces planned state and contracts; planning alone does not execute a payment or confirm an external outcome.

`requestPolicy`, `policyAction`, `policyWatches` and `requestStep` are declared extension functions without implementations here. They supply the policy, action name, additional watched paths and request step. This type therefore establishes the gate mechanism without specifying a particular payment action, actor or request payload.

## Conditional policy

`plan` first builds the inherited connection plan. It adds conditional behavior only when the policy returned by `requestPolicy` has `mode: "when"`. An absent `mode` defaults to `"workflow"`; any value other than `"when"` returns the connection plan unchanged.

For `"when"` mode:

- `when` is the policy predicate. `parameters/sources`, read from `/clauseRuntime/work/candidate/<clauseKey>`, defaults to `{}` and declares aliases used by predicate references under `/sources/<alias>`.
- The plan initializes `/paymentProcess_<clauseKey>/<action>Allowed` to `false`, where `<action>` is returned by `policyAction`.
- `/paymentTerms/<action>Gate` stores the pointer to that Boolean. An existing different pointer rejects planning with `PAYMENT_POLICY_GATE_CONFLICT`. The planned `/paymentTerms` replacement preserves its other current fields.
- Each path returned by `policyWatches` and each document path found in `when` receives an update-channel handler. Nonempty `parameters/sources` additionally creates an Embedded Node Channel handler without a `sourcePath` filter.

Each generated handler evaluates whether `/activation/active` is exactly `true`, whether `/clauses/documentSources` is absent or `/sourceLinks/ready` is exactly `true`, and whether `when` evaluates to exactly `true`. It stages a gate replacement only when the Boolean changes, then runs the step supplied by `requestStep` with the gate pointer and policy. That second step is present regardless of the computed Boolean; any suppression of requests belongs to its implementation.

These paths belong to the document executing the generated steps. The gate represents computed eligibility, not payment completion or personal permission. Its planned initial `false` is not a rule for interpreting missing state; an absent stored value remains unknown. Activation or readiness alone does not establish that a handler has run.

## Predicate constraints

Dependency scanning permits `$document`, `$eq`, `$ne`, `$lt`, `$lte`, `$gt`, `$gte`, `$and`, `$or`, `$not`, `$exists`, `$includes`, `$size`, `$add`, `$subtract`, `$literal`, and the operand keys `list` and `val`. Other object keys reject planning with `PAYMENT_PREDICATE_REQUIRES_STATIC_PURE_DEPENDENCIES`. `$literal` contents are not scanned.

Every scanned `$document` operand must be literal text starting with `/`, other than `/` itself; otherwise planning fails with `PAYMENT_PREDICATE_STATIC_PATH_REQUIRED`. References starting with `/sources/` require a declared alias or fail with `PAYMENT_PREDICATE_SOURCE_NOT_DECLARED`. Scanning processes 33 levels, including the root, and rejects remaining descendants with `PAYMENT_PREDICATE_TOO_DEEP`.

## Inherited connections

`bindings` override `type/defaultBindings`. Property bindings must match `type/bindingTypes`; omission is allowed only for names in `type/optionalBindings`. Pointer bindings must be non-root absolute paths. Action bindings are dictionaries of named connections. Clause, action and connection names must be nonempty and contain no `.`, `/` or `~`; unknown bindings and unsupported connection fields are rejected.

Actions come from `type/actions`, or `parameters/actions` when `type/configurableActions` is `true`. A type may instead declare structural `type/initialState`. `type/embeds` and `type/embedsCollections` require declared pointer bindings; `type/snapshotBindings` captures existing values during planning. A supplied action `automatic` connection reserves the name `_automatic`.

Connections select sources through `on`: `event`, `embedded`, `collection`, `change`, `channel`, `initialized`, `activated`, `workflow` or `timer`. Source-specific fields include `event`, `path` and `channel`; `workflow` uses `party` in preference to `channel` and may declare `request`. Embedded and collection sources contribute processing paths unless `embed` is explicitly `false`. Collection handlers ignore events outside the configured path’s descendants.

Action `defaults` are merged with connection `params`. Connection `when` defaults to `true` and skips execution when unsatisfied. Argument checks, action `require/when` and `parameters/conditions/<action>` precede execution; failed requirements reject the attempt. Optional `preflight` precedes `before`, action `do` and `after`. Preflight requires an explicit `actionResult.outcome`; `resultContract: "outcome-v1"` requires one after `do` as well. Accepted values are `acceptedNew`, `duplicate`, `rejected` and `skipped`; only `acceptedNew` continues. `resultContract` defaults to `"legacy"`.

`once` defaults to `false`. Connection state at `/connectionState_<clauseKey>/<action>.<connection>` starts with `armed: false` and `fired: false`. A `once` connection sets `fired` only after reaching the end of its action sequence and subsequently skips execution. This records connection progress, not an external business outcome.

Timer connections require exactly one of `timestamp` or `afterEvent`. Absolute `timestamp` is an integer Unix time in microseconds, from 0 through 9007199254740991, armed on initialization; it forbids `delayMs` and `policy`. Relative timers require a timestamped source and positive integer `delayMs` up to 9007199254740. Their `policy` defaults to `"first"`, suppressing further arming once `armed` is true; `"latest"` emits replacements. `cancelOn` must name a nonempty source. Cancellation emits a keyed cancellation request; the generated code does not reset `armed`. Timer requests require the Time runtime, and committed scheduling is distinct from an admitted firing.

## Validation and outcomes

`validateConfiguration` calls `validateConnectionsConfiguration` and `requestPolicy`, then returns the connection validation result. The inherited validation function returns `allowed: true`; additional checks occur during planning. `validateTransition` always returns `allowed: false` with `PAYMENT_PROCESS_POLICY_IMMUTABLE`.

The request step’s authorization, rejection rules and external outcome handling are unspecified here. Neither an allowed gate nor an emitted request establishes a completed payment.
